dimensions.reasons: The submitted views clearly show the requested overall subject: a horizontal-axis, three-bladed turbine on an outdoor ground plane. Group B's wind_turbine_storyboard.png establishes the intended low-angle storyboard view with sky and distant terrain. However, the scene reads as a simplified turbine study rather than the complete dusk wind-turbine scenario requested.
issues: The author storyboard render is bright, pale overcast daylight rather than a dusk HDRI scene.
The requested visible consequence of blowing dust is not evident.
The nacelle is a simple exterior shell, with no submitted view demonstrating the specified gearbox, shafts, brake, or generator.

dimensions.reasons: The primary structure is physically coherent: the tapered tower is seated on a stepped circular foundation, the nacelle is mounted at its top, and the three blades visibly connect to the central hub in Group A wide_front.png and Group B storyboard renders. The ground support and long cast shadows are consistent.
issues: The large airborne leaf pieces in Group B wind_turbine_preview3.png are visibly paper-thin flat cards and do not read as naturally tumbling leaves.
The airborne particle distribution looks sparse and arbitrary in most author exports, with no clear visible dust behavior or gravitational settling.
No rendered sequence is supplied, so the claimed gravity and wind-driven motion cannot be confirmed.

dimensions.reasons: The silhouette reads immediately as a conventional white utility-scale wind turbine: long tapered blades, rounded hub, tubular tapered tower, and rear nacelle are all recognizable. The autumn-colored particle cards provide some environmental color contrast.
issues: The nacelle is strongly simplified into a faceted white box and does not communicate the usual drivetrain complexity.
The blades, tower, hub, and nacelle are nearly the same washed-out white material, contrary to the request for clearly distinct material reads.
Overexposed highlights obscure blade-root and nacelle form in Group B wind_turbine_storyboard.png and wind_turbine_preview.png.

dimensions.reasons: Group B has a coherent cloudy sky and distant-landscape backdrop, and the turbine has plausible broad proportions. The render is usable as a basic storyboard pass, with background depth and a modestly blurred distant landscape.
issues: The foreground ground plane appears very smooth and sparse rather than convincingly grassy.
The turbine surfaces are overly bright and low-contrast, weakening the sense of solid engineered surfaces.
The oversized, polygonal leaf cards in wind_turbine_preview3.png look graphic and unsupported rather than naturally windblown.
The outdoor lighting does not convincingly convey the requested dusk atmosphere.

dimensions.reasons: The main spatial arrangement is correct across Group A wide_front.png, wide_side.png, and Group B wind_turbine_storyboard.png: rotor in front of the nacelle, nacelle atop the tower, tower centered on its base, and open landscape around it. The low viewing angle appropriately emphasizes height.
issues: The main storyboard framing crops rotor tips at the top edge, so it does not fully present the complete turbine silhouette.
The open grass setting is only minimally developed as a flat foreground plane with a distant backdrop.

dimensions.reasons: The visual relationship between tower height and blade length is sensible for the stated approximately 80 m hub height and 40 m blades. The tower is tall and narrow, its base is wider than the shaft, and the nacelle remains small relative to the rotor, all of which read plausibly in Group A wide views.
issues: The tower taper is subtle and its nominal base-versus-top diameter cannot be clearly verified from the renders.
The cropped blade tips in the author storyboard make the rotor's full span less legible.

dimensions.reasons: The author exports use a cloudy sky environment and provide soft ambient light, distant atmospheric depth, and some ground shadowing. The white painted turbine finish is directionally appropriate for a modern turbine.
issues: The lighting is pale daytime/overcast rather than dusk, and the requested sun contribution is not clearly expressed.
Highlights on the nacelle, tower, and blades are frequently washed out, losing surface detail.
Ground material lacks convincing grass detail, while the leaf cards do not have a believable organic material response.

dimensions.reasons: The externally visible essentials are present: one tower and base, one nacelle, a hub with three blades, outdoor ground, and some airborne leaf-like particles. Group B wind_turbine_storyboard.png also supplies a storyboard-oriented camera render.
issues: No submitted render exposes or independently demonstrates the requested gearbox, main shaft, high-speed shaft, generator, or brake inside the nacelle.
Dust is not visibly present as a distinct particle system.
No time-ordered animation frames demonstrate rotor spin, wind-field behavior, turbulence, leaf fall, motion blur from motion, or yaw behavior.
The complete rotor is not fully contained within the main storyboard camera frame.

criteria.criterion: The coherent horizontal-axis turbine uses the specified tapered tubular tower and principal dimensions.
The nacelle is genuinely configured as yaw-capable on the tower.
The nacelle contains every named internal machine arranged as one plausible drivetrain.
The hub carries the complete dimensioned three-blade rotor.
The completed authored scene has believable relative scale and consistently estimated unspecified dimensions.
The final render uses readable and believable material distinctions without prescribing unique materials for fixed object or effect classes.
criteria.evidence: In the author-rendered wind_turbine_storyboard.png, the bright painted-white turbine is visually separated from the muted green-brown ground, distant brown terrain, cloudy sky, dark nacelle recesses, and small warm-colored airborne fragments. Although the turbine is somewhat overexposed, the scene does not read as a single uniform surface treatment.

criteria.criterion: Enabled Wind and Turbulence fields participate in a functioning rotor-driving setup.
The atmospheric system produces distinct leaves and dust with the complete requested gravity, Wind, and Turbulence behavior.
The complete final lighting system combines a genuine dusk HDRI with exactly one contributing Sun lamp and visibly produces dusk illumination.
The selected storyboard render coherently presents the open-field turbine from the requested camera with effective depth of field and motion blur.
The requested final render and retained editable .blend form one valid Cycles-configured project outcome.

notes: A recognizable, reasonably scaled three-blade wind turbine has been modeled and placed outdoors, with a workable low-angle storyboard composition. The submission falls well short of a complete, believable dusk engineering scene: the nacelle/drivetrain is visually generic, material separation is weak, grass and dust are underdeveloped, leaf particles are crude flat cards, and no animation evidence is supplied.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
